task: Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed. Open the door, then pick up the box in the other room.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the task commands 'Open the door, then pick up the box' — both events are required unconditionally and as hard requirements — but the candidate's only hard clause is Response(door_open, target_picked_up), a rule that requires nothing and leaves FINAL_STATES empty; the rule-only warning does not apply because 'open' and 'pick up' are imperative commands. Replace the Response with hard Existence(target_picked_up) and hard Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up): together they force the door to be opened and put it before the box pickup, so no Existence(door_open) is needed. Keep the soft Absence(key_lost), which correctly captures the preference 'try not to drop the key while the door is still closed' (key_lost already encodes the door-closed condition).

NO CHANGES NEEDED: Absence(key_lost) soft matches 'try not to drop the key while the door is still closed' — the key_lost definition already contains the 'while the door is closed' condition, so a plain soft Absence is right. Existence(target_picked_up) hard with Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) hard captures 'Open the door, then pick up the box': the hard Existence of the last step plus the Precedence forces door_open, so no Existence(door_open) is needed.
